senses.gloss:
Khandaparitta(than)
Bud. Pāli. From Samyuttanikāya (?). Colombo D. I. 268-70. 272-83. [Page180-b]
See also Malalasekera, Dict. of Pāli Proper Names I. p. 71.

Khandhakakathā
Pkt. Jain. included in Kathāsaṅgraha. Pattan I. p. 61.

Khandhavagga
from Saṁyuttanikāya. Fausboll 50. 53.
Ed.. L. Feer, PTS. 1890.
Mentioned along with a Ṭīkā on it in a. ins. d. 1442 a. Pagan.
See Bode, Pāli Lit. of Burma, p. 103; J. Myth. Soc. XXII. p. 40.

Khānakhāna_Abdur_Rahīm
(1557-1630 A. D.) warrior, courtier an. writer under Akbar, patron of poets; himself credited with some works in Hindi an. in mixed Hindi cum Skt.
See Khan-i-Khanan an. Sanskrit Learning, J. B. Chaudhuri. Calcutta, 1954.
--Kheṭakautuka. jy.
Pt.. Veṅk. Press, Bombay, 1936-37.
--Gaṅgāṣṭaka in Skt. Printed on the basis of a ms. in Bharatpur, in the Skt. [Page184-a. magazine, Saṅgamanī, Allahabad, II. ii. p.. 89-91.
--Madanāṣṭaka in Mālinī. available in two versions.
Pt.. (1) in Nāgarī Pracāriṇī Patrikā. (2) Sammelan Patrikā, Bhadra, 1922.
--Rahīmkāvya.
See p.. 10-11, 19-23, Khan-i-Khanan an. Sanskrit Learning.
--other stray verses.
See ibid.
Under him flourished--
--Kṛṣṇadaivajña, a. of Jātakapaddhatyudāharaṇa.
See NCC. IV. p. 323b.
--Rudrakavi, a. of Nawab Khān Khānancarita. (Pt.. p.. 63-80, J. B. Chaudhury, ibid.), Kīrtisamullāsa, Rāṣṭrauḍhavaṁśa kāvya an. other works.

Khāna_Ravicandrakalādhara
name of a commentator on Amaruśataka found in a Dacca ms. an. in a ms. with Sri Dinesh Chandra Bhattacharya.
See Our Heritage II. i. 1954 p. 13. fn. 2 (khAna zrIravicandra eSa instead of zrI lakSmIravicandra eSa).

Khāntaramiśra
father an. teacher of Mm. Mādhava Miśra; q.s from his work found in Mādhava's C. on Jayadeva's [Page184-b] Āloka; ms. in Darbhanga Raj Library.
See History of Navya Nyāya in Mithila, p.. 183-4.
